analysis.summary_en: In December 2024 and early January 2025, China reported increased acute respiratory infections with increased detections of seasonal influenza, rhinovirus, RSV and hMPV during the Northern Hemisphere winter. To rapidly generate nationwide situational data without overburdening laboratories already performing routine respiratory virus surveillance, each site was asked to test up to five eligible SARI samples per week for hMPV from January to April 2025. title: The Resurgence of Respiratory Viruses After COVID-19: Molecular Insights from Pediatric SARI in Kashmir.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory viruses are major causes of severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) in children, yet molecular epidemiology data from northern India, particularly after the COVID-19 pandemic, remain sparse. This study addressed the knowledge gap by determining the prevalence and distribution of respiratory viral pathogens among hospitalized pediatric SARI patients in Kashmir.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective study was conducted from October 2023 to April 2025 at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar. Children aged ≤15 years meeting the World Health Organization SARI case definition were enrolled, yielding a total of 326 cases.
analysis.methods: Nasopharyngeal and/or oropharyngeal samples were collected and tested using real-time polymerase chain reaction assays for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B, Respiratory Syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, Adenovirus, Human metapneumovirus, Rhinovirus, and Para-influenza viruses.
analysis.main_results: At least one respiratory virus was detected in 200 patients (61.3%). RSV was the most frequently detected virus, with RSV-B identified in 111 cases (34.0%) and RSV-A in 26 cases (7.9%). Influenza viruses accounted for a smaller proportion, including influenza A(H1N1) in 12 cases (3.6%), influenza A(H3N2) in 6 cases (1.8%), and influenza B (Victoria lineage) in 21 cases (6.4%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as showing that respiratory viruses account for a substantial proportion of pediatric SARI cases in Kashmir, with RSV emerging as the predominant pathogen in the post-pandemic period. This study provides new molecular insights into the resurgence of respiratory viruses in a previously understudied region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strengthening molecular surveillance may improve diagnostic stewardship and guide targeted prevention strategies for pediatric SARI in Kashmir.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-centre design and lack of a control group, which may affect generalisability. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on a well-defined but geographically restricted cohort and robust molecular methods.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective study investigated the molecular epidemiology of respiratory viruses among 326 pediatric severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases in Kashmir from October 2023 to April 2025. Using real-time PCR assays, at least one respiratory virus was detected in 61.3% of cases, with Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) being the most prevalent (41.9% combined RSV-A and RSV-B). Influenza viruses were less common, comprising 11.8% of detections. Most infections occurred in winter and predominantly affected infants. The authors conclude that respiratory viruses, particularly RSV, account for a substantial burden of pediatric SARI in the post-COVID-19 period, highlighting the need for enhanced molecular surveillance and targeted prevention strategies.

analysis.summary_en: ABSTRACT We evaluated the antiviral activity of a library of 36 urea-based small-molecule cyclophilin inhibitors (SMCypIs) against human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV). The supplied evidence does not clearly state the study design, setting, or study population. Beyond its dual efficacy, F832/33 displayed strong antiviral activity against additional clinically relevant respiratory pathogens, including parainfluenza virus type 3, enterovirus D68, and both ancestral and Omicron severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 strains, in immortalized cell lines and fully differentiated human nasal epithelial cells, a physiologically relevant model of respiratory infection. Structure–spectrum analysis revealed virus-specific structural requirements for antiviral efficacy. Collectively, our results demonstrate that structure–activity relationship-guided optimization can be successfully applied to expand the antiviral spectrum of SMCypIs, positioning F832/33 as a promising host-targeted broad-spectrum antiviral candidate. Further in vivo studies are warranted to evaluate its therapeutic potential and clarify its precise mechanism of action. Competition assays with alisporivir confirmed that the antiviral effects of SMCypIs depend on their specific interaction with Cyp.

title: Comparative evaluation of classical and machine learning methods for medical image enhancement

analysis.methods: Our findings statistically validate that although classical operators remain highly effective for specific boundary detection tasks, machine learning (ML) frameworks provide the most robust performance for cross-modality image enhancement, bridging the gap between raw data acquisition and clinical interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: Medical imaging is critical for diagnostic accuracy, yet raw images often suffer from noise and low contrast. This study provides a comparative evaluation of classical methods, namely the Laplace transform (LT), Sobel operator (SO), and histogram equalization (HE), against a data-driven convolutional neural network (CNN) using the musculoskeletal radiographs (MURA) and Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) lung computed tomography (CT) datasets. Our findings statistically validate that although classical operators remain highly effective for specific boundary detection tasks, machine learning (ML) frameworks provide the most robust performance for cross-modality image enhancement, bridging the gap between raw data acquisition and clinical interpretation. In contrast, the CNN based approach demonstrates superior detail preservation and entropy, offering a more balanced and adaptive solution for diverse diagnostic requirements. While quantitative analysis shows that HE and SO significantly outperform other methods in isolated contrast enhancement and edge definition, they often introduce artifacts.
